name: LuaJIT x64 without GC64: every GC allocation must satisfy (addr >> 31) == 0, i.e. the whole Lua heap lives below 2 GiB
required_postconditions: (returned_address >> 31) == 0 and ((returned_address + size) >> 31) == 0, so the arena ends strictly below 0x80000000
any mapping that violates this is munmapped again and the probe retries, up to 30 times
the first strategy is mmap(NULL-ish, MAP_32BIT); the source itself notes 'This only allows 1GB on Linux. So fallback to probing to get 2GB.'

failure_sink.description: after 30 failed probes mmap_probe returns MFAIL ((void*)~0). The allocator turns that into an allocation failure, which surfaces to the script as a Lua out-of-memory error. Recoverable in principle, fatal to the VM in practice.

source_locations.symbol: #define LJ_ALLOC_MBITS 31 /* 2 GB on x64 with !LJ_GC64. */  (guard: #elif LJ_TARGET_X64, inside #if LJ_64, under #if LJ_GC64/#elif)
comment: '/* Due to limitations in the x64 non-GC64 VM. */'
#define LJ_ALLOC_MBITS 47 /* 128 TB in LJ_GC64 mode. */ - the SAME program is a completely different contract when built with GC64
if ((addr >> LJ_ALLOC_MBITS) == 0 && addr >= LJ_ALLOC_MMAP_PROBE_LOWER && ((addr + size) >> LJ_ALLOC_MBITS) == 0)
mmap((void *)LJ_ALLOC_MMAP32_START, size, MMAP_PROT, MAP_32BIT|MMAP_FLAGS, -1, 0) - LJ_ALLOC_MMAP32_START is 0 except on Solaris (0x1000)
uint32_t gcptr32; /* Pseudo 32 bit pointer. */ - the storage slot that forces the 2 GiB bound

extraction_limitations: the constants MMAP_REGION_START and MMAP_REGION_END do NOT exist at this commit; they were the LuaJIT 2.0 spelling. The live mechanism is LJ_ALLOC_MBITS plus the probe loop, and that is what is modelled here.

the real requirement is an upper bound on the returned address (< 2^31), which this schema cannot state. pointer_storage_width_bits=32 is the closest field and is only an approximation: the true bound is 2^31, not 2^32, and LuaJIT rejects-and-retries rather than truncating.
size 131072 is DEFAULT_GRANULARITY, the unit the allocator requests; individual Lua objects are carved out of it.

x_campaign.rationale: x86-64 Linux does provide MAP_32BIT and honours low hints, so this configuration ships and works; but an unconstrained mmap returns ~0x7f.. and the program depends entirely on its probe loop landing low, which is a conditional property of the host, not a guarantee.
x_campaign.note_after_schema_fix: LJ_ALLOC_MBITS is an address bound the program TESTS and rejects, not a pointer-width truncation.
